clue.text: A superficial figure only half a cleric and he all confused.

parts.note: semi- is the prefix meaning half, as in semi-detached

indicators.note: the letters of the word cleric are thoroughly muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A geometry lesson muddled with a churchman who is himself thoroughly mixed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superficial' here means 'of a surface', so a flat geometric figure; the surface tempts you to read it as shallow.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-round shape is a plane figure, one drawn on a surface, hence superficial in the old geometric sense.

clue.text: This worry could be of an Irish variety.

definitions.meaning: to be in a fret or state of anxiety

definitions.text: could be of an Irish variety
definitions.meaning: a dish of meat and vegetables simmered slowly, Irish being a famous kind

explanation.surface: A fretful mood that turns out to have an Irish flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: Irish stew is a mutton, potato and onion casserole.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a stew is to be anxious, and a stew is a slowly simmered dish.

clue.text: The kind of status acquired from a Union.

definitions.text: The kind of status acquired from a Union.

parts.words: The kind of status acquired from a Union.
parts.note: Union sounds political, like a trade union or a nation, but it means a wedding, which changes the status asked for on forms

explanation.surface: A question of the standing one gains by joining a union.
explanation.definitionFit: Forms ask whether one is single or wed, the status a marriage confers.

clue.text: Histrionic hors d'oeuvre?

parts.note: a theatrical starter: the short play performed before the main show, as an appetiser comes before the main course

explanation.surface: A melodramatic appetiser.
explanation.definitionFit: A short opening piece staged before the main play is the theatre's equivalent of a starter.

clue.text: Perhaps 1.dn, was, but she heard otherwise.

indicators.note: in another way, so the letters of she heard are set out differently

explanation.surface: Someone says a dish was cooked one way, but she heard it differently.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 down is STEW, a dish often served up again from leftovers; 'otherwise' reorders SHE HEARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A stew warmed up and served again from leftovers has been reheated and re-served.

clue.text: A: hell which is evidently something more than calf love.

parts.note: the calf is only part of a leg, so the larger thing is a limb
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A claim that a hellish state is clearly more serious than puppy love.
explanation.walkthrough: Calf love is youthful infatuation; here 'calf' is the leg muscle. In theology, the place of limbo borders hell.
explanation.definitionFit: The abode of unbaptised souls on the edge of the underworld, loosely a kind of perdition.

clue.text: Backward 101 ounce animal.

indicators.note: placed in front of the pieces, it tells the solver to read the whole run from right to left

parts.note: 101 in Roman numerals is CI

explanation.surface: A backward big cat, an ounce being a snow leopard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' turns CIOZ round. The ounce is also the snow leopard, which makes 'animal' look like its description.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means pertaining to living creatures, as in Mesozoic and Palaeozoic.

clue.text: The, occasion has gone by (or has it?) for this sort of dance.

definitions.text: The, occasion has gone by (or has it?) for this sort of dance.

parts.words: The, occasion has gone by (or has it?) for this sort of dance.
parts.note: an era that has passed, yet dancers still enjoy its ballroom style, so its day is both over and not over

explanation.surface: A wistful remark that the moment for a certain dance may or may not be past.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-fashioned ballroom dancing such as the waltz and the veleta is called by this name.

clue.text: Those anxious to make a settlement.

definitions.text: Those anxious to make a settlement.

parts.words: Those anxious to make a settlement.
parts.note: reads like people keen to settle a debt or dispute, but means people founding a new outpost abroad

explanation.surface: People eager to settle out of court.
explanation.definitionFit: Founders of a colony set up a new settlement in foreign territory.

clue.text: Alternative to mistake, yet still a mistake.

indicators.note: means attached to, so the second piece goes after the first

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Choosing another option instead of a blunder still turns out to be a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunder or slip is a mistake.

clue.text: O child, am I so deranged as to be murderous?

indicators.note: deranged means thrown out of order, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A parent asks a child whether they are mad enough to kill.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a tendency to kill is the same as being murderous.

clue.text: Jack sometimes takes one or two for himself here.

definitions.text: Jack sometimes takes one or two for himself here.

parts.words: Jack sometimes takes one or two for himself here.
parts.note: Jack looks like a greedy man, but is the playing card: in a card game it scores one point for his nob or two for his heels, pegged on a holed scoring device

explanation.surface: A man named Jack helping himself to a few.
explanation.definitionFit: Cribbage is scored with pegs on a holed board, and the jack earns one or two points.

clue.text: Putting across a key reorganisation.

definitions.meaning: moving something to a different place, swapping positions
rewriting music in a different musical key

explanation.surface: Communicating a crucial restructuring.
explanation.definitionFit: Shifting things into new positions, or recasting a piece into another musical key, both carry the name.

clue.text: A follower who takes a light vehicle in chase.

indicators.note: the light vehicle is placed inside the word for the chase

parts.note: a chase is a pursuit
a van is a light goods vehicle

explanation.surface: A hanger-on who joins a pursuit by van.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior heraldic officer, or more generally an attendant, follows a superior.

clue.text: Hill-dweller gets the soil in a pure mixture.

indicators.note: the soil goes inside the jumbled letters
a mixture blends things, so the letters of pure are mixed up

parts.note: land is soil or ground

explanation.surface: A highland farmer gets his earth into a clean blend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hill-dweller' is the definition at the front; 'gets' and 'a' are link words in a 1960s-style surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living in high hill country is a highlander, a dweller on the heights.

clue.text: The sailor allows, of course, for these white river fish.

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
lets means allows

explanation.surface: A sailor permits, naturally, some little freshwater fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The ablet is the bleak, a small silvery freshwater fish.

clue.text: Administers a thrashing, but a medicine man within survives.

indicators.note: the doctor goes inside the word for survives

parts.note: lasts means survives or endures
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor

explanation.surface: Someone gives a beating, but a doctor on hand pulls through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medicine man' suggests a shaman, but it is a qualified doctor with an MB degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Beating someone soundly, or attacking verbally, means thrashing them.

clue.text: Mother's taken aback at the vessel-a Chinese one.

indicators.note: taken back means turned around, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: Mother is MA, with the possessive S
a pan is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: Mum is startled at the sight of a Chinese boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' looks like surprise but turns MAS into SAM. 'one' refers to a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: This flat-bottomed boat is a typical small craft of Chinese rivers and harbours.

clue.text: Just the place for a glass of wine and a piece of cake.

definitions.text: Just the place for a glass of wine
definitions.meaning: the Atlantic island that gives its name to a fortified wine
a plain sponge cake traditionally eaten with that wine

explanation.surface: A suggestion of somewhere ideal for wine and cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is the Portuguese island, its fortified wine, and the sponge cake once served with it.

clue.text: Gran gets rough!

indicators.note: roughly handled, so the letters of gran gets are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Grandmother turns violent.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and a picture of a granny turned thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent criminal is the sort who would get rough.

clue.text: It's contained yonder-in either Einstein or Newton.

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something is held in the theory of Einstein or Newton.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is inside eiTHER EINstein; 'or Newton' completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in that place or thing, so something held there is in it.

clue.text: Enid's distress with the crate and broken bale can't be explained.

indicators.note: distressed means damaged or roughed up, so the letters are put in another order

parts.note: the name with its possessive S, used as five letters
a crib is a box or crate, as for fodder

indicators.note: broken apart, so the letters of bale are rearranged

explanation.surface: Enid is upset when the crate and the bale both fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distress' turns ENIDS into INDES; 'broken' turns BALE into ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond description cannot be put into words.

clue.text: This ambitious fellow's sometimes 'quite revolting.

parts.note: a person who climbs in the world, but one who rises up can also be a rebel rising against authority

explanation.surface: An ambitious man can be rather disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rises in the world, or rises in revolt, fits both senses.

clue.text: Prop and stop?

definitions.meaning: to halt or remain in place

explanation.surface: Two terse instructions to a theatre crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope or brace that supports a mast is so called, and to halt or remain is to linger.

clue.text: They make a bee-line for the honey.

definitions.text: They make a bee-line for the honey.

parts.words: They make a bee-line for the honey.
parts.note: reads as greedy people rushing to something sweet, but describes keepers of hives who go to collect it

explanation.surface: People who rush straight to sweet things.
explanation.definitionFit: Beekeepers keep hives and harvest honey from them.

clue.text: On the watch for a later development.

indicators.note: something developing changes form, so the letters of the word later take a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone keeps an eye out for news that will come later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development' rearranges LATER; 'for a' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being watchful and wide awake to danger is being vigilant.

clue.text: A drop that could be a ripping affair.

definitions.meaning: a drop of liquid shed from the eye when crying
a rip or rent in fabric

explanation.surface: A drop that might also be a splendid occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ripping' looks like old slang for splendid, but means tearing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a droplet from the eye and a rip in cloth.

clue.text: Denis and Percy work well together in high office.

indicators.note: the letters of the two names are worked into one blended arrangement

explanation.surface: Two colleagues named Denis and Percy cooperate in a senior post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work well together' rearranges DENIS and PERCY.
explanation.definitionFit: The role of leading a country or organisation is a top post.
